articles.title: Rowhammer Backdoor Injection Attack During Inference (Northeastern)
articles.summary: Researchers from Northeastern University published a technical paper titled “ROBBIN: Rowhammer-Based Backdoor Injection during Inference.” Abstract excerpt: “This work presents ROBBIN, a hardware-aware Rowhammer-based backdoor injection attack that integrates the device-specific vulnerability into the backdoor construction process. ROBBIN first characterizes the bit-flip patterns of a target DRAM and uses this information to iteratively select DRAM page mappings for the model weights that would maximize ASR while preserving TA under Rowhammering. By treating every hammering-induced bit-flip as an integral part of the attack design rather than first constructing a hardware-agnostic backdoor and dismissing collateral flips as side effects, ROBBIN produces backdoors that remain robust a

articles.title: Affirm CEO: American Consumers Are Healthy

articles.title: The Pixel 11 Pro’s HiLight feature looks cool, but it’s missing 5 big features
articles.summary: I miss the days when notification LEDs were a thing. I still remember the red light flashing on my BlackBerry whenever a notification came in. I’d immediately pick up my phone and check what I’d missed. Smartphones have mostly left that idea behind. Yes, Nothing did bring it back in its own way with the Glyph lights, but personally, that feels like a little too much of a light show. That’s why Google’s HiLight feature on the Pixel 11 Pro series immediately caught my attention. It feels like a much more modern take on the notification LED I used to love. The light sits neatly inside the camera visor; it can glow in different colors, and it’s quite subtle. But the problem is, after using HiLight, I can’t stop thinking about how much more useful it could be .

articles.title: I need to stop using the Galaxy Z Fold 8, but I can’t
articles.summary: It’s been nearly two weeks since I first put my SIM in the Galaxy Z Fold 8 . I got some hands-on time with the device before picking one up, so I largely knew what to expect. However, what I didn’t anticipate was not wanting to use any other phone afterward. I test over 40 smartphones a year, and I desperately need to move on to other devices, but I’m just having too much fun with the Galaxy Z Fold 8. If you’re using the Galaxy Z Fold 8, you know the feeling extends beyond the initial honeymoon phase. The phone has flaws, and I can easily point them out. However, the mark of an excellent phone is that I look beyond them.

articles.title: I rely on Google Maps every day, but these 4 missing features still hold it back
articles.summary: Over the past two decades, Google Maps has evolved from a simple navigation app into a tool I use for almost everything. From my daily commute to helping me find nearby coffee shops and business opening hours, to providing live traffic information so I can figure out when I need to leave for my destination, the feature set has expanded by leaps and bounds. But despite all those updates, redesigns, and AI additions, there are still some features I wish Google Maps had added . None of these features require a ground-up rethink. Instead, these are simple quality-of-life tools that would make Maps more useful for people who rely on it every day.

articles.title: Commits on GitHub have doubled in four months. Verification capacity has not.
articles.summary: I have been waiting for agent-generated code to show up in public infrastructure data rather than in vendor benchmarks. In August, it did. GitHub now handles 2.9 billion commits a month and says it cannot keep up . Monthly commit volume more than doubled in four months , from 1.4 billion in April to 2.9 billion in August. The growth broke the platform. On August 17, GitHub went down for 7 hours and 47 minutes after a core infrastructure component in its Central US data center failed to scale with traffic. The postmortem from CTO Vladimir Fedorov did not hedge: If you were trying to ship software that day, GitHub let you down. The remediation is what a hyperscaler does when demand outruns supply. articles.title: Meta Child Safety Deal Puts Rivals on Notice
articles.summary: Meta’s child safety settlement includes new protections for young users and is increasing pressure on other social media platforms to adopt similar safeguards. UK House of Lords National Security Strategy Committee member and Online Safety Activist Baroness Beeban Kidron is on Bloomberg This Weekend and says the bigger impact may come from forcing technology companies to take greater responsibility for product design and age verification, rather than relying on children and parents to protect themselves. (Source: Bloomberg)

articles.title: Inside the Dangote Family Vision and the Next Era of African Industry
articles.summary: What does the future hold for one of Africa's most powerful industrial empires? In this exclusive conversation on Bloomberg Next Africa, Halima, Mariya, and Fatima Dangote sit down to discuss the next generation of leadership at the Dangote Group — from expanding cement production and investing in refining, fertilizer and power to building a family office focused on preserving the family’s legacy for generations. They also discuss creating more value from Africa’s resources at home, the role of partnerships and investment, and plans for a pan-African IPO of the Dangote refinery. Discover how Aliko Dangote’s daughters plan to carry forward their father's legacy through strategic growth, diversification, and long-term wealth preservation. (Source: Bloomberg)

articles.title: I asked 100 companies for my data. Some deleted it instead.
articles.summary: I filed a request with McDonald’s earlier this month to access all of the personal data the fast food company collected about me, and I received a stunning 515-page report a few days later that detailed my app interactions in granular detail and predicted I would never stop eating there. Under the California Consumer Privacy Act , I have the legal right to request access to information from large companies that collect personal data. So I was curious what others might have on me, and I spent the next week filing more than 100 requests. The CCPA went into effect in 2020, and three of its key provisions are the right to opt out of the selling of personal information, the right to delete that info, and the right to request a copy for yourself. Read full article Comments
